issues.description: The problem statement requires a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon, but the solution implements a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This name/signature mismatch will confuse students about which method to implement and will cause tests or graders that expect acceptSupplyDelivery to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent with the problem statement. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery (keeping parameters (String name, int price, int quantity) and static visibility), or update the problem statement and UML to use receiveDelivery instead. Ensure the template/test expectations use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template Main refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(...) on SealSaloon, but the solution implementation provides a static method named receiveDelivery(...) instead. This inconsistent method name for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery and updating the shared stock) creates confusion for students: they are instructed to implement/expect acceptSupplyDelivery, the template example calls acceptSupplyDelivery, yet the reference solution exposes receiveDelivery. Students may implement the method using the name from the problem/template and find a mismatch with the solution or tests that use the other name.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the static delivery-accepting method across all artifacts. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery(...) to acceptSupplyDelivery(...) (signature: public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)) so it matches the problem statement and the template Main example — or alternatively, update the problem statement and template to use receiveDelivery if that name is preferred. Ensure Main and tests use the same chosen name.
